record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the compressible Euler equations in higher space dimensions, what is the correct well-posedness theory for physically relevant weak solutions? This includes identifying appropriate functional spaces, describing the geometric structure and interactions of generic discontinuities, formulating the right entropy conditions, determining the asymptotic stability of planar shock waves and centered rarefaction waves under non-planar perturbations, and deciding when existence, uniqueness, or compactness of the solution operator should hold.

evidence.quote: The well-posedness of weak solutions. The well-posedness of weak solutions to the compressible Euler equations in higher space dimensions remains to be one of the most challenging open problems for mathematical theory of compressible fluid dynamics.

What are the geometric structures of generic discontinuities in a weak solution? How do the basic linear and nonlinear waves evolve and interact? What are the appropriate entropy conditions? Are the planar shock waves ... and centered rarefactions waves asymptotically stable under non-planary perturbations? What is the appropriate space in which one can obtain either existence (even for short time) or uniqueness of general physically relevant weak solutions? When is the solution operator compact?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the compressible Euler equations in $d \ge 2$ space dimensions for an ideal gas:
\[
\partial_t \rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho u) = 0, \qquad \partial_t(\rho u) + \nabla\cdot(\rho u\otimes u) + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \partial_t E + \nabla\cdot((E+p)u) = 0,
\]
where $\rho>0$ is the density, $u\in\mathbb{R}^d$ the velocity, $p$ the pressure, and $E=\tfrac12\rho|u|^2+\rho e$ the total energy, with an equation of state $p=p(\rho,e)$ (e.g.\ polytropic $p=(\gamma-1)\rho e$, $\gamma>1$). A weak solution is a locally integrable triple $(\rho,u,e)$ satisfying these equations in the sense of distributions and an admissibility (entropy) inequality of the form $\partial_t(\rho s)+\nabla\cdot(\rho s u)\ge 0$ for an appropriate entropy $s$.

Develop a well-posedness theory for physically relevant weak solutions of this system. Specifically:
(a) Identify a function space $X$ of initial data and a corresponding solution space in which existence (even short-time) and/or uniqueness of weak admissible solutions can be established.
(b) Describe the geometric structure of generic discontinuities (shocks, contact discontinuities, vortex sheets) in such weak solutions and the manner in which linear and nonlinear waves evolve and interact.
(c) Formulate the correct entropy/admissibility conditions that single out physically relevant solutions and rule out the non-uniqueness phenomena produced by convex integration.
(d) Determine whether planar shock waves and centered rarefaction waves are asymptotically stable under multidimensional, non-planar perturbations.
(e) Determine conditions under which the solution operator (initial data $\mapsto$ solution at time $t$) is compact on $X$.
artifact.status_search_result: The multidimensional well-posedness theory for the compressible Euler equations is widely regarded as one of the central open problems in mathematical fluid dynamics. Recent work using convex integration (De Lellis–Székelyhidi, Chiodaroli, Buckmaster and collaborators) has shown non-uniqueness of bounded admissible weak solutions, deepening rather than resolving the problem; stability of planar shocks/rarefactions under multi-D perturbations and the search for adequate function spaces and entropy criteria remain active areas of research as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: On Admissibility Criteria for Weak Solutions of the Euler Equations
status_evidence.snippet: De Lellis and Székelyhidi show non-uniqueness of admissible weak solutions to multidimensional Euler equations.
status_evidence.claim: Standard entropy admissibility does not yield uniqueness for multi-D Euler, showing the open status of well-posedness.

status_evidence.title: Non-uniqueness of admissible weak solutions to the compressible Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: Chiodaroli, De Lellis, Kreml construct non-unique admissible weak solutions to compressible Euler with Lipschitz initial data.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that the well-posedness problem remains open with current entropy conditions.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: The well-posedness of weak solutions to the compressible Euler equations in higher space dimensions remains one of the most challenging open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as open.
